questionText:
Which of the following predicate logic formulae/formula is/are CORRECT representation(s) of the statement: “Everyone has exactly one mother”?

The meanings of the predicates used are:
• $mother(y, x)$: $y$ is the mother of $x$
• $noteq(x, y)$: $x$ and $y$ are not equal
options: $\forall x \exists y \exists z (mother(y, x) \land \neg mother(z, x))$
$\forall x \exists y [mother(y, x) \land \forall z (noteq(z, y) \rightarrow \neg mother(z, x))]$
$\forall x \forall y [mother(y, x) \rightarrow \exists z (mother(z, x) \land \neg noteq(z, y))]$
$\forall x \exists y [mother(y, x) \land \neg \exists z (noteq(z, y) \land mother(z, x))]$
explanation:
To represent the statement "Everyone has exactly one mother", we need to express two conditions for every person $x$:
1. Existence: There exists a person $y$ such that $y$ is the mother of $x$, i.e., $mother(y, x)$.
2. Uniqueness: Any person $z$ who is not equal to $y$ ($noteq(z, y)$) is not the mother of $x$ ($ eg mother(z, x)$). Alternatively, there does not exist any person $z$ who is different from $y$ and is also the mother of $x$.

Analysis of options:

• Option (B): $ orall x \exists y [mother(y, x) \land orall z (noteq(z, y) ightarrow eg mother(z, x))]
This directly captures both existence ($mother(y, x)$) and uniqueness (if $z eq y$, then $z$ is not the mother of $x$). Thus, Option (B) is CORRECT.

• Option (D): $ orall x \exists y [mother(y, x) \land eg \exists z (noteq(z, y) \land mother(z, x))]
Notice that $ orall z (noteq(z, y) ightarrow eg mother(z, x))$ is logically equivalent to $ orall z ( eg noteq(z, y) \lor eg mother(z, x)) \equiv eg \exists z (noteq(z, y) \land mother(z, x))$. Thus, Option (D) is CORRECT.

• Option (A): Incorrect because it does not properly link $z$ to being distinct from $y$.
• Option (C): Incorrect because it uses universal quantifiers incorrectly for existence.
